response.title: Should I buy one big battery power station or add an extra battery to the one I have for longer outages?
response.answer:
I'd generally recommend adding an expansion battery to your existing power station rather than buying a completely new, larger one—provided your current station supports expansion and has enough power output for your needs.

For longer power outages, the most important distinction is between battery capacity (Wh) and power output (W).

Capacity (Wh or kWh) determines how long your appliances can run.

Output (W) determines which appliances you can power and how many you can run simultaneously.

An expansion battery typically increases capacity without increasing output. A larger power station may improve both.

Which option is better?

For multi-day outages, redundancy matters. If your existing power station fails, an attached expansion battery may be unusable. Having two independent power stations can be valuable, especially when you're relying on them for refrigeration, communications, or other essentials.

One important consideration: for outages lasting several days, recharging capability may matter more than simply buying more battery capacity. Solar panels or another safe charging source can extend backup power substantially.

Two questions so I can recommend the better purchase

What brand and model power station do you currently own? (For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max, Anker SOLIX F2000, or BLUETTI AC200L.)

What do you want to keep running during an outage? Just a refrigerator, internet and lights, or also appliances such as an air conditioner?

With those details, I can compare the actual expansion-battery cost against buying a second station, including cost per kWh, expected runtime and redundancy.

**I'd generally recommend adding an expansion battery to your existing power station rather than buying a completely new, larger one**—provided your current station supports expansion and has enough power output for your needs.

For longer power outages, the most important distinction is between **battery capacity (Wh)** and **power output (W)**.

- **Capacity (Wh or kWh)** determines how long your appliances can run.
- **Output (W)** determines which appliances you can power and how many you can run simultaneously.

An expansion battery typically increases capacity without increasing output. A larger power station may improve both.

## Which option is better?

| Factor | Add an expansion battery | Buy a larger power station |
|---|---|---|
| Cost per extra kWh | Often better | Often higher |
| Backup runtime | Longer | Longer |
| Maximum power output | Usually unchanged | Potentially higher |
| Portability | Modular, but more pieces | Often heavier |
| Redundancy | Still depends on main station | Two independent stations if you keep the old one |
| Flexibility | Limited to compatible batteries | More options |

For multi-day outages, **redundancy matters**. If your existing power station fails, an attached expansion battery may be unusable. Having two independent power stations can be valuable, especially when you're relying on them for refrigeration, communications, or other essentials.

## How much extra runtime would you get?

Here's an illustrative estimate for a constant 150W average load, assuming 85% usable energy:

{@body const [load,setLoad] = DIL.useState(150)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState(2000)}
{@body const [extra,setExtra] = DIL.useState(2000)}
{@body const hours = wh => wh*.85/load}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Estimate your backup runtime</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Average appliance load</text>
    **{load} W**
  </row>
  <slider min={50} max={600} step={25} value={load} onChange={setLoad}/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Existing capacity</text>
      <select block size="md" value={String(capacity)} onChange={v=>setCapacity(Number(v))} options={[{label:"1 kWh",value:"1000"},{label:"2 kWh",value:"2000"},{label:"3 kWh",value:"3000"},{label:"4 kWh",value:"4000"}]}/>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Expansion capacity</text>
      <select block size="md" value={String(extra)} onChange={v=>setExtra(Number(v))} options={[{label:"1 kWh",value:"1000"},{label:"2 kWh",value:"2000"},{label:"3 kWh",value:"3000"},{label:"4 kWh",value:"4000"}]}/>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">Current runtime</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{hours(capacity).toFixed(1)} hrs</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
        <text color="secondary" size="xs">With expansion</text>
        <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{hours(capacity+extra).toFixed(1)} hrs</title>
      </box>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>Approximate runtime only; actual results vary with inverter losses, standby consumption, appliance cycling and battery condition.</caption>
</box>

One important consideration: for outages lasting several days, **recharging capability may matter more than simply buying more battery capacity**. Solar panels or another safe charging source can extend backup power substantially. <Cite refs={["turn503750search1","turn503750search9"]}/>
